text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Choose **Mistral’s 8x22B mixture-of-experts** for EXCAVA’s core LLM workloads. It delivers near-top-tier performance at half the compute cost of dense models, freeing budget for faster iteration and more data. The trade-off is higher latency on some queries, but the speed gain in training and fine-tuning outweighs it for our use case.

name: Torque
text: Mistral’s 8x22B locks EXCAVA into a paid MoE stack—its free tier is capped, and the 8x GPU memory hit means we either overpay or throttle throughput. Swap it for **Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct**—free, dense, and tops benchmarks in its class with no vendor trap; if latency matters, run it on Cerebras CS-3’s free tier to test. Settle it with a 24-hour bake-off: same prompt set, same hardware, measure tokens/sec and accuracy—no opinions, just numbers.

name: Torque
text: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct’s "free" label hides a real risk: its dense architecture demands 72B parameters on a single GPU, capping throughput on anything short of a high-end A100/H100 cluster—most teams hit a wall at batch size 1. Push instead for **DeepSeek-V3** (671B MoE, but free and gated only by compute, not vendor): it delivers Mistral-level speed with near-Qwen accuracy, and the open weights let us shard it across cheaper GPUs without throttling. Settle it with a 24-hour bake-off: run both on identical hardware, log tokens/sec and latency—if DeepSeek beats Qwen on throughput without sacrificing quality, it’s the call.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run DeepSeek-V3 (671B MoE) on Cerebras CS-3 for 48-hour benchmark—Torque owns the artifact proving its throughput vs. Qwen2.5-72B on EXCAVA’s core workloads.
